title: A FINE BLEND
author: Bill Haufe
content:
A FINE BLEND

 September 4, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 846
 Words 

 Read News Document

 CENTREVILLE — Brian Mooney likes the blend Queen Anne's County High's football team has going this preseason.The Lions' second-year head coach likes how his offensive spread game is mixing with the return of former head coach Donny Graef's double-wing approach.
Mooney likes that his offense returns rock-solid 1,000-plus yard rusher John Connolly and sophomore sensation Ja'Dereon Thompson. He likes how his almost new offensive line is coming together under Graef's tutelage.
Mooney also likes his defensive blend, where he and Graef have been molding ends Amari Baynard and Conlan Nagle, where the electric Thompson and two-time all-Bayside Conference corner Carter Dickey are again roaming the secondary, and where Parker Whiteford — after a year at DeMatha — has returned in an alpha role at inside linebacker.
"It's a work in progress," said Mooney, who went 6-5 a year ago. "We're transitioning."
Perhaps the biggest transition is on offense, where Graef, the school's winningest head coach — compiling a 176-95 record over 25 years — returns as an assistant. Among Graef's duties will be coaching the offensive line, which was the longtime domain of another Lions' coaching great, Dave Perillo, now at Easton.
"We have a brand new line," said Mooney, noting senior Nate Mayoral did get a couple spot starts last season. "He's the only one with varsity starting experience. All those guys are cutting their teeth under coach Graef which is awesome.
Centering that line will be 5-foot-11, 225-pound junior Drew Sutton. Juniors Brian Maleski (5-10, 185) and Mac Windsor (6-foot, 210) line up at guard, though senior Ethan Wheaton (5-10, 195) figures to be worked in. Junior Elijah Goldsborough (6-4, 280) is at right tackle and Mayoral (6-3, 260) is on the left side.
"To learn from a Hall of Famer is an awesome opportunity for those guys," Mooney said of his offensive front which includes senior tight ends Christian St. Germain (5-11, 190) and Whiteford (6-1, 215). "They're really soaking it in. Coach Graef, he has high expectations, and when they don't meet those expectations he holds them to it. It's really cool to watch that blend with the skills we have."
The Lions' skill group looks strong. Junior Lance Arnold (5-10, 180), who started the last six games a year ago, returns at quarterback, with sophomore Carter Hercher (6-0, 190) at backup.
A first-time all-conference pick a year ago, Connolly (6-0, 210), a senior, returns to lead a backfield that includes juniors Dorrin Phillips (5-9, 195) and Dickey (5-8, 155), and sophomore Hunter Kelly (5-9, 170).
"We have some skill guys that are going to make any offensive line look good," Mooney said. "John Connolly, we expect to lean on him very heavily."
But as far as play calling goes, Mooney plans to balance his spread philosophy with Graef's old-school style.
"We're kind of working on doing some things Coach Graef is more familiar with," Mooney said. "Bringing him in as offensive line coach makes sense to go back to doing a lot of the things we were successful doing before. It's been a good blend."
Adding to that blend is a receiving corps that includes juniors Baynard (6-4, 190) and Brooks Blodgett (6-0, 175), and senior Nagle (6-2, 190). But the biggest threat is Thompson.
"Ja'Dereon obviously is a human highlight reel," Mooney said.
Thompson is also a threat to blaze into the end zone every time he handles a kick. Last year as a freshman he averaged 41 yards on kickoff returns, taking three in for touchdowns, and 25 yards on punt returns, which included one touchdown.
"He's a blessing to have," Mooney said of Thompson. "And the way he practice and carries himself. I mean some of the stuff you see. ... I always tell the college coaches I talk to, if you could see his practice tape you'd offer him right now."
The Lions look to have more experience on defense, where Thompson returns at deep safety in a secondary that features Dickey and Kelly at strong safety, Blodgett and junior Wyatt Wilhoit (5-8, 155) at corner, and Hercher, who can be inserted at corner or safety.
Wheaton returns at starting tackle and is joined by Sutton, who had spot starts last year, and Goldsborough, who can give either a break when needed. Bookending that trio are ends Baynard and Nagle.
The biggest boost to the defense though figures to be the return of Whiteford at inside linebacker, where he plays along side senior Frank Constantino (5-9, 210) and Maleski.
"The linebacker core, Parker being an alpha, being that coach on the field, he always has them in the right spots, and he makes up if they mess up," Mooney said. "He's just a downhill dynamo. We're excited about having a kid like that patrolling the middle of our defense."
Nagle will kick and punt, though Mooney said Ethan Kepler, a goalie on the soccer team, could also do some place-kicking throughout the season. The Lions also have Michaels Simmons, who goes from being team manager a year ago, to this year's long snapper on punts and kicks.
"We expect to have some bumps and bruises along the way," Mooney said. "But it's going to be fun to see."

Defending North Bayside champion Queen Anne’s County among teams trying to fill graduation holes in an attempt for another deep playoff

 September 17, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 1620
 Words 

 Read News Document

 North Bayside boys soccer coaches have been busy this preseason — and during the early weeks of the regular season — mending holes in their lineups.Defending division champion Queen Anne's County High, which went 13-3-1 and reached the Class 2A state semifinals a year ago, graduated eight, including six starters.
"The guys that we lost were huge parts," Lions head coach Wade Hosler said.
North Caroline head coach John Austin can sympathize after graduating seven, including 2023 North Bayside Player of the Year Logan Harned.
"I feel as a conference we lost a lot of really good players," Austin said. "Last year's conference was very, very senior heavy."
A handful of those graduates are now playing in the collegiate ranks, with North Caroline's Harned at Neumann (Pa.) University and goalie Gavin O'Brien at Frostburg State, while Queen Anne's has Billy Schindler at Washington College.
The Class 1A ranks also felt graduation's sting. North Dorchester lost 10, while Cambridge-South Dorchester first-year head coach Josh Dohoney is trying to patch holes created by almost half of dozen losses.
In addition to the Vikings, Easton welcomes former standout Avery Brice as its new head coach, while Kent County begins the Dennis Hickman era.
Queen Anne's shared the conference title with James M. Bennett in 2021, but the last North team to win the Bayside championship outright was Kent Island in 2016, when the Bucs topped Stephen Decatur in penalty kicks. The Bucs and Lions look to be on another collision course to decide the North when they meet in Stevensville on Oct. 18, though North Caroline and Easton figure to also be atop the division ranks.
The South's dominance of the conference crown could be extended this year, as Bennett, which lost to eventual Class 3A state champion South River in last year's postseason, returns the bulk of its team from a season ago.
Here's a look at this year's North Bayside teams.
CAMBRIDGE-SD
Head Coach: Josh Dohoney.
Who's Where: Goalie: Nate Huber (Sr.); Backs: Osvaldo Hernandez (Jr.); Evan Kozak (Sr.); Colton Phillips (So.); Gibby Robinson (So.); Midfield: Lucas Harper (So.); Gavin Weber (So.); Ryan Harris (Sr.); Forwards: Will Banks (Jr.); Wyatt Abbott (So.); Marcos Hernandez (Fr.).
Outlook: After one year as an assistant, Dohoney begins his first head coaching job in soccer knowing he'll need to be patient.
"We're very young. Very much a rebuilding squad," said Dohoney, who played at Delmar, Del.
The Vikings graduated more than half a dozen from last year, including center midfielder Randall Johnson. The midfield looks technically sound, but with five sophomores and one freshman starting, Dohoney hopes this will be a season of growth.
COL. RICHARDSON
Head Coach: Dillon Shaheen.
Who's Where: Goalie: Cohen Carels (Sr.); Backs: Cameron Todd (Sr.); Jacklin Novembre (Jr.); Jackson Jean Jr. (Jr.); Caleb Rouser (So.); Midfield: John Beaven (So.); Jack Walls (Jr.); Preston Rickwood (Sr.); Ludver Vasquez (Jr.); Aydan Downie (Sr.); Forwards: Morgan Demir (Sr.); Angel Castro-Rios (Sr.); Skyler Endzel (Fr.); Brody Omohundro (Fr.).
Outlook: Shaheen begins his third year as head coach with his most experienced team he's had. That has translated into victories over Pocomoke and North Dorchester for starters.
"It's been pretty good so far," said Shaheen, who lost three seniors from last year. "Obviously we have a lot of seniors and juniors, and most have been playing at the varsity level for three or four years. I'm pretty confident in our squad this year."
EASTON
Head Coach: Avery Brice.
Who's Where: Goalie: Sam Hutchison (Jr.); Backs: Mario Medina (Sr.); Felix Valentine (Jr.); Brody Byrnes (Sr.); Kai Ferraris (Jr.); Landon Chaney (Sr.); Midfield: Clay Nagle (Sr.); Luke Stanco (Jr.); CJ Chaconas (Sr.); Blake Royer (So.); Ale Monroy (So.); Dominic Stanco (Sr.); Otto Perez-Arreaga (Fr.); Logan Sundt (Jr.); Liam Edgell (Sr.); Forwards: Kyle Ensminger (Jr.); Rodi Fresco Rubio (Jr.).
Outlook: Brice was a center midfielder on Easton's last two teams to win Bayside titles (2013, '14) and helped the Warriors reach the 2A state final in '14 before continuing his playing career at Wesley (Del.) College.
Now, he steps into his first head coaching job.
"Things are shaping up nicely," Brice said. "Could things be better? Yes. That's kind of one thing that we just hope to do every day in the season; just be better than the day before."
While the Warriors have been receptive to their new coach's ideas and style, Brice stressed they must strive for consistency.
"The mindset is you can be really good, but every game you've got to bring it," Brice said.
KENT COUNTY
Head Coach: Dennis Hickman.
Who's Where: Goalie: Leyder Cruz (Sr.); Backs: Noah Iacona (Jr.); Jayden Miller (So.); Stewart Hickman (Jr.); Bryce Jacobs (So.); Midfield: Nick Stead (Sr.); Colbyn Lopez (Jr.); Ethan Clark (Sr.); Forwards: Gabe Parr (So.); Dylan Peralta (Fr.); Sebastian Cousineau (So.).
Outlook: A 1993 graduate of Kent County, Hickman, who played soccer, baseball and wrestled for the Trojans, takes over as head coach after spending the last two years as an assistant.
In an attempt to build a program, Hickman has already achieved one goal in fielding a junior varsity for the first time since 2019.
"We think by having a jayvee, getting them out there on practice, getting them those reps and having some game-time situations and play, that we're only going to be able to build on that moving forward," Hickman said. "It's just the best thing for the program."
That coupled with a varsity roster that includes nine juniors and nine sophomores, could bode well for the future.
As for this year's team, there isn't a lot of experience, though Stewart Hickman has plenty of travel ball experience, as has recruited players over the summer to come out for the team.
KENT ISLAND
Head Coach: Lin Outten.
Who's Where: Goalie: Quinn Burns (Fr.); Backs: Davis Miller (Sr.); Noah Scopp (Sr.); Gavin Neboshynsky (Sr.); Mark Rees (Sr.); Spencer Chappell (Jr.); Elijah James (So.); Midfield: Simon Vujinovic (Sr.); Brendan Thomas (Jr.); Cooper Liebel (So.); Landon Pecor (Jr.); Forwards: AJ Miller (Jr.); Eric Hoffman (Sr.); Ethan Schriver (Sr.); Robert Simkins (Jr.).
Outlook: The Bucs have a lot of experience moving from the midfield into the attack, but are not as experienced in the back. Though seniors Davis Miller, Scopp and Rees return, Outten hopes shifting Neboshynsky and Chappell from midfield to the back bolsters his defense.
AJ Miller netted 10 goals a year ago, and Outten thinks that number will go up, especially with the return of Hoffman, who missed the bulk of last year with an early season injury.
"But really what makes the engine go is the three guys in the middle — Thomas, Vujinovic and Liebel," Outten said.
NORTH CAROLINE
Head Coach: John Austin.
Who's Where: Goalie: Mason Shilling (Jr.); Backs: Lewis Higgs (Jr.); Brayden Boarts (Sr.); Jimmy Cohoon (Jr.); Midfield: Ayden Russell (Jr.); Tyler Gutierrez (Jr.); Omar Marroquin (Sr.); Jonnathan Luna Feliciano (Jr.); Diego Castro (So.); Landyn Harned (So.); Kyle Reed (Jr.); Forwards: Heath Frantum (Jr.); Issac Bautista (Jr.); Luke Raga (So.).
Outlook: The Bulldogs graduated seven from a year ago, including Harned, O'Brien, and also lost leading scorer Kevin Godinez.
Austin thinks his team will be more defensive-minded this season. The defense is led by Shilling, who Austin thinks has college potential. Shilling and company figure to be tested early, as the Bulldogs open with defending conference champion James M. Bennett, Class 2A state semifinalist Queen Anne's, and perennial conference heavyweight Stephen Decatur.
"We have a lot of holes to fill," Austin said. "I think we are where we need to be right now. But the goal is can we just keep getting better as the year goes on, and then when October rolls around, play our best soccer?"
NORTH DORCHESTER
Head Coach: Gabe Guzman.
Who's Where: Goalie: Jayden Coleman (Jr.); Backs: Chris Sanchez (Jr.); Tahjere Pritchett (Jr.); Alex Fonseca-Gonzalez (So.); Martin Chirino Fernandez (Jr.); Midfield: Christian Chase (Jr.); Peyton Bleyer (So.); Daniel Mejia (Sr.); Kegan Henry (Jr.); Forwards: Volcy Nerat (Fr.); Dagoberto Chirino Fernandez.
Outlook: The Eagles graduated 10, including seven starters. Among Guzman's top priorities is getting his freshman to buy into his system and get acclimated to the high school varsity format.
"We're working on trust," Guzman said.
QUEEN ANNE'S
Head Coach: Wade Hosler.
Who's Where: Goalie: Ethan Keppler (Sr.); Backs: Christian Coppage (Sr.); Conner Cheezum (Sr.); Hayden Albright (Sr.); Brody Nordvik (Jr.); Midfield: James Rath (Jr.); Gage Jordan (Sr.); Nathan Kostka (Jr.); Mason Albright (Sr.); Boden Blodgett (So.); Josiah Hegarty (So.); Forwards: Ryan Lee (Sr.).
Outlook: "The preseason seemed awfully short this year, and our chemistry wasn't quite where I'd like it this time of year," Hosler said. "But I think it's coming, so I'm optimistic that we can do good things. We've had good moments and we've had mistakes. But I like the direction we're heading in."
Hosler has also liked his team's 3-0-1 start, which included Monday's 3-0 shutout of North Caroline.
Despite its big graduation losses, the Lions do have a solid core of returners. Outside backs Coppage and Cheezum return along with Keppler in goal. Jordan is back in the midfield while Lee returns at striker.
"We have some big pieces, but we still have some big holes to fill," said Hosler, who graduation losses included Schindler, center back William Nagle and leading scorer Nick Esper. "If we can have some guys step up I think we'll be OK."
ST. MICHAELS
Head Coach: Pat Hambleton.
Who's Where: Goalie: Will Sherwood (Sr.); Backs: Tyler Murphy (Jr.); Jack Brennan (Sr.); Sherwin Mendez (Sr.); Brennan Dean (Jr.); Midfield: Ethan Royer (Jr.); Gavin Bieber (Fr.); Johnny Mautz (Jr.); Abel Delgaudio (So.); Forwards: Connor Wheeler (Jr.); Miles Fox (Jr.); Haven Haddaway (Sr.).
Outlook: Having Sherwood — first-team all-North Bayside goalie the past two years — and an experienced returning defensive unit should make the Saints plenty tough.
While that provides Hambleton comfort, he also liked what he has seen on the offensive end.
"Finally creative," Hambleton said of his attack. "We're going to be an enjoyment to watch. Still have an older group to support our creative offensive style. I have players to make it a pretty game finally. And they get it."

title: Mautz' first goal proves to be game-winner for Saints
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Mautz' first goal proves to be game-winner for Saints

 September 25, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 708
 Words 

 Read News Document

 ST. MICHAELS — Johnny Mautz hadn't played high school soccer before this season.Judging by the celebration he triggered midway through Tuesday night's second half, his St. Michaels High teammates are elated he decided to give the game a go this season.
Ethan Royer crossed a ball that Mautz converted into what proved to be the game-winning goal, as the Saints rallied from a halftime deficit to notch a 3-2 victory over Class 1A rival and previously unbeaten Colonel Richardson.
"I was playing baseball for awhile but I just stopped playing last year," said Mautz, a standout on the Saints' basketball team. "I never played soccer 'cause I didn't want to play three sports. But I said I might as well come out because I was only playing one sport (basketball). And then the rest is history."
There was also a touch of history attached to Mautz' score.
"That was his first goal of the year," St. Michaels head coach Pat Hambleton said of Mautz. "He's hit the post six times."
That strike with 21 minutes, 9 seconds remaining not only capped a three-goal, second-half surge, giving St. Michaels a 3-1 lead, but it also afforded the Saints (3-2 overall, 2-1 North Bayside) the breathing room they needed to weather Colonels' late-game push.
Not quite 4 minutes after having a goal erased by an offsides call, Colonel (4-1, 2-1) took a 1-0 lead on Aydan Downie's unassisted tally with 9:42 left in the first half.
St. Michaels' best chance to pull even came with just under 2 minutes to go in the first half, when Miles Fox put a shot right on Colonel keeper Cohen Carels, who made a midsection stop.
The Saints pulled even though just 1:26 into the second half, when Sherwin Mendez parked a direct kick into the back of the net for a 1-all tie.
"I think their free kick a minute and a half into the second half definitely gave them some momentum," Colonel head coach Dillon Shaheen said. "And they took that and ran with it."
Not quite 10 minutes later, Fox got deep on the left wing and steered a crossing pass that Connor Wheeler banged into the net for a 2-1 St. Michaels lead.
"Their sweeper was playing a little too far back I noticed," Hambleton said. "He was solely intercepting through balls, so I just made a small adjustment, where once he left for that through ball, I had a forward there, and it happened to be Connor. So he left, peeled off to Miles. Miles received and played that ball across, and it was wide open in the front of the net. It was just a good momentum boost that we needed to start the half."
Less than 8 minutes later, Royer slid a pass from the left side through the crease to the right post and a waiting Mautz for a 3-1 lead.
"I've been working on staying back post so that I can get whatever comes my way," Mautz said. "And Ethan played me a beautiful ball and I was just right there for the lefty finish."
Colonel wasn't quite finished though.
With 15:06 remaining, St. Michaels was called for a handball in the box. Colonel's Angel Castro Rios calmly deposited the penalty kick to the left of St. Michaels keeper Lucas Greenwood to make it a one-goal difference.
With Colonel continuing to push into the Saints' end, Hambleton dropped his team into defensive mode. St. Michaels foiled rushes and generally got in the way over the final 12 minutes, with Colonel's best chance for the equalizer coming with 6:37 left, when Greenwood smothered a loose ball near the left post in front of a charging Downie.
"Energy. They definitely came out a little more ready than we were, and we talked to them about that at halftime," Shaheen said. "I think they wanted the ball more it seemed. We match up pretty well with them, and they know they match up well with us. What it usually comes down to is which ever team plays harder, and they were definitely that team."
NORTH CAROLINE 8 CAMBRIDGE-SD 0
CAMBRIDGE — Omar Marroquin had a hat trick as the Bulldogs earned their first win of the season.
North Caroline (1-4, 1-2) also got goals from Mason Shilling, Adrian Lopez Rivera, Brayden Boarts, Karson Hollingworth and Jimmy Cohoon.

title: Queen Anne's sweeps past Easton
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Queen Anne's sweeps past Easton

 October 2, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 616
 Words 

 Read News Document

 EASTON — The view from college to the high school game has been somewhat of a transition for Jamie Leventry."The growth of the players at the high school level is fun to see. We can really see it," said Leventry, Queen Anne's County High's first-year head volleyball coach, who last year was coaching at Washington College. "When I was in college, you really had to grind hard on some players to get them to have basically incremental improvements, whereas here, every week we get better. And it's a lot of fun to be back doing that."
Two nights after an emotional victory over Kent Island, the Lions registered their seventh sweep of the season Wednesday, grinding their way past Easton, 25-23, 25-20, 25-15 to remain unbeaten.
"We played so hard on Monday and it really took a lot out of us," Leventry said of Queen Anne's 3-1 victory over Kent Island, leaving the Lions (8-0 overall) alone in first place atop the North Bayside Division at 7-0. "Even at practice (Tuesday) we were a little sluggish. But we pushed through. It wasn't pretty but we pushed through."
Queen Anne's appeared ready to answer their coaches plea for a fast start when it built a 6-2 lead in Game 1. But a kill by Easton's Sofia Stecher-Roberts pulled the Warriors (3-5, 2-5) even at 9-9. Stecher-Roberts tapped down a kill and converted two service points to give Easton a 15-11 lead. Three times Queen Anne's rallied to tie before a block by Elizabeth Darling pushed the Lions in front at 21-20.
The Warriors took a 23-22 lead on a Lions' mishit. But a Bianca Baker kill and two errant Easton returns sealed Game 1 for the Lions.
Easton took an early lead in Game 2 behind Sacoya Williams' four-point service run, which included an ace. But Marylee Kline's six-point run from the service line nudged Queen Anne's to an 8-6 lead. The match would be tied five times before Baker hammered a winner that gave the Lions a lead they never surrendered at 17-16. And though Alli Dill's back-to-back winners clinched the 25-20 victory for Queen Anne's in the second game, Easton first-year head coach Scott Walstrum was pleased with his team's play.
"My big concern was that we'd lose focus mid-set and they didn't," Walstrum said. "We've been getting to mid-set and the bottom has been falling out. But tonight the girls played all the way through.
"Queen Anne's is a great team, and a lot of teams can be intimidated by that," Walstrum added. "But our girls had nothing to lose and they put everything out there, and I couldn't be more proud. They played all the way to 25."
Game 3 featured only one tie — that coming at 1-1 — as Queen Anne's steadily built a lead before the Warriors sent a return into the net to complete the 10-point, third-set victory for the defending Bayside Conference champions.
"I think our volleyball IQ is getting higher, and we're serving and passing well," Leventry said of a team that again features heavy hitters Sydney Pinder and Baker. "Then the others can contribute as well. Libs (Liberty Ott) has had some big games for us. We've got some depth."
The Lions have the type of poise they showed last year on the way to winning the Bayside and regional titles.
"That's kind of our goal this year was really just stay at a high level; not to get too up or down," Leventry said. "Just play at a good level. And we've had some opportunities this year where we were down a little bit but still started playing at a high level and were able to come back and win. It's nice that we're there."

title: RS Shooting Sports celebrates third anniversary with continued focus on youth sports
author: ERIC SYLVIA Special to the Star Democrat
content:
RS Shooting Sports celebrates third anniversary with continued focus on youth sports

 October 4, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: ERIC SYLVIA Special to the Star Democrat | Section: Business 
 
 437
 Words 

 Read News Document

 CHESTER — Owners of RS Shooting Sports Scott Gray and Robbie Frey invited the community to celebrate the business's three year anniversary and get a glimpse of the future.Joining the celebration at 110 D Country Day Rd. in Chester were coaches and student athletes from three area high schools that Gray and Frey are sponsoring as they compete in the Maryland State High School Clay Target League.
Gray and Frey set out to establish a different kind of gun shop, focused on establishing a community for the shooting sports enthusiasts in the area, and have succeeded in building a thriving business, growing steadily the past three years. Now entering its fourth year at this location, RSSS has expanded, adding a training facility for a myriad of courses.
In addition to the classes offered at the store, the shop also offers engraving services, full-service gunsmithing, on-site Cerakote services and Custom Kydex Holsters to fit any firearm. They are now running monthly classes for a number of firearms permits including the Maryland Handgun Wear and Carry Permit.
The two owners were happy to help the first Eastern Shore high school clay team — the Kent Island team is recognized as being the first public school in Maryland to join the USA High School Clay Target League and was followed soon after with the establishment of the club at Queen Anne's County High. They helped the team get established, and their commitment to the local shooting community has expanded with the introduction of a clay targets team at Easton High School.
Speaking with volunteer coach Joe Cap, he said, "we have stressed to our team that this is not just about shooting. They are required to attend and participate in community functions." Cap continued, "Just last week they attended the school board meeting, and the students provided them with an update."
In an email chat with QACHS coach Nathan Powell, he spelled out the underlying strategy, saying, "The continual development and evolution of our program is building young adults who are active in our communities and developing critical leadership skills to continue to grow and contribute beyond the high school environment."
"Additionally, we have tapped into a population of student athletes who do not always fit the traditional sports model or mold," Powell continued. "Our program has given them purpose, focus and direction that extends away from the sports environment, into the classroom, the home and the community."
Also joining in the festivities was Marine Corp recruiter Mark Winkles, who challenged guests with a chin-up challenge. Pupuseria Kent Island was on hand to feed the masses, along with tasty treats from AB Made Sweets and Treats.

title: Next-man-up approach still working for QA's
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Next-man-up approach still working for QA's

 October 8, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 837
 Words 

 Read News Document

 It was just another weekend for Queen Anne's County High's football team.It was another game tainted by injury. Wait, make that injuries.
And yet despite losing two defensive starters and their starting quarterback, the Lions again found a way to log another victory last Friday, stretching their win streak to three with a convincing 43-6 rout of North Caroline.
"Hats off to our defensive coordinator, coach Jude Mandes," Queen Anne's head coach Brian Mooney said after the Lions registered their most lopsided victory of the season while holding North Caroline to a season-low six points. "He does a great job of mixing up his coverages and the looks that he gives defenses. He's been really dialed in with his blitz packages as of late. He's continuing to grow just like our defense."
Also continuing to grow is the Lions' injury list.
On the first play of the game Friday, starting defensive end Conlan Nagle got rolled up on, suffering a leg injury. Amari Baynard stepped in for Nagle.
All-Bayside Conference starting safety Carter Dickey injured his arm during the second defensive series. Sophomore Alex McDonald went in for Dickey and got his first playing time of the year, and "played really well," Mooney said.
The defense got another outstanding effort from inside linebacker Parker Whiteford (10 tackles).
"They moved the ball on us pretty good that first drive, but he's just an alpha," Mooney said of Whiteford. "He's just a man-child. I don't know what else to say about the kid. It's an awesome treat to have. Him and coach Jude have a great unison and between the two of them, he's kind of like another Jude out on the field."
Mooney also praised the play of junior cornerback Wyatt Wilhoit, who finished with six tackles, including a sack, and a forced fumble.
"Kind of getting his first varsity experience, he had a great night," Mooney said of Wilhoit. "Had a forced fumble inside the 20 on one of their first drives, and then I think he had the game-changing play. Right before halftime they were driving (to Queen Anne's 30) and he came off the edge on one of coach's blitzes and just cracked the quarterback for about a 10-yard loss. It just kind of changed the whole momentum of the game I felt."
Queen Anne's then lost starting quarterback Carter Hercher, who got hurt while attempting a pass in the third quarter.
Before getting injured, Hercher had completed 6 of 7 passes for 104 yards, and carried three times for 11 yards.
The Lions didn't stall though, moving sophomore Ja'Dereon Thompson behind center in the wildcat formation. Thompson finished the game with touchdown runs of 25 and 40 yards as part of a six-carry, 92-yard rushing effort, and caught two passes for 62 yards.
"We call it the flashback with Ja'Dereon, and we've been practicing that just in case something like that happened," Mooney said. "And he went in and we didn't miss a beat."
Senior running back John Connolly also didn't miss a beat, as he carried 16 times for 190 yards, with touchdown runs of 1, 10 and 11 yards.
"We've been really working on his technique, some of his footwork stuff in the week leading up, and he just hit it on a tee," Mooney said of Connolly. "He was cutting really well behind the guards on power and finding that groove. He was averaging 11 yards a carry. We're going to ride our guy."
Queen Anne's hosts Kent County (1-4) for homecoming on Saturday at noon.
NO PANICDespite Friday's 38-0 loss at defending Class 2A state champion Stephen Decatur, Easton head coach Matt Griffith doesn't see his team unraveling.
"Obviously it was not what we expected," Griffith said after the Warriors slipped to 4-1. "We expected to give them a game at least. We did early."
The Seahawks (5-0) were up 7-0, scored early in the second quarter, then erupted for three more touchdowns in the final 5:02 before halftime.
"There was a tipped ball that goes off a receiver's hands, and we had some debacles up front driving," Griffith said. "Again, good football team. They've got some great athletes. We just didn't execute our part. If we want a chance to redeem ourselves we have to play really good and redeem ourselves against them maybe in the postseason."
Easton was held to 12 rushing yards on 11 attempts, and senior quarterback Mikey O'Connor completed 7 of 20 passes or a season-low 27 yards.
"We didn't respond in a big game, big atmosphere," Griffith said. "And while Decatur's a very good football team we did not play our best football. And this game does not dictate the season. You get to dictate the rest of the season and that starts (last) Saturday morning.
Easton hosts Parkside (2-3) on Friday at 6:30 p.m.
BUCS STOPPEDThe surprise from last weekend may have been Wicomico's 21-14 upset of Kent Island on Saturday in Stevensville. Bucs quarterback Gavan Henry completed 10 of 25 passes for 122 yards and a touchdown to Jackson Towers, and running back Jaxson Hess finished with 12 carries for 44 yards and a touchdown.

title: North Caroline fires head football coach
author: Bill Haufe
content:
North Caroline fires head football coach

 October 9, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 482
 Words 

 Read News Document

 Nic McMorris was fired Monday morning as North Caroline High's head football coach midway through his second season.The Bulldogs went 9-2 and reached the second round of the Class 2A East Region playoffs last year in McMorris' first season as head coach. The team was expected to have another strong season this year, with running backs Zymear Smith and Tyson Weber, and all-Bayside Conference defensive end Owen Piavis returning.
But the Bulldogs have struggled, falling to 0-5 after last Friday night's 43-6 loss at Queen Anne's, their most lopsided loss of the season.
McMorris said he received a phone call Monday morning from North Caroline principal Matt Spiker, who wanted to schedule a face-to-face meeting with the head coach.
"I will say he tried to have me in the office. He tried to have a face-to-face conversation," McMorris said Wednesday morning during a phone interview. "I wanted to have a conversation right then and there, so we talked on the phone. I was in St. Michaels, and I was like, 'I don't want to be thinking about this for an hour and a half.'"
McMorris said Spiker told him he was being let go as head football coach. McMorris did not say why he was let go.
Reached by phone Wednesday morning, Spiker declined to comment, referring the matter to Caroline County Public Schools public information officer Sandi Barry.
"Mr. McMorris is no longer employed by CCPS (Caroline County Public Schools), however we wish him success in future endeavors," Barry said, reading from a statement. "As with all personnel matters, we cannot provide any further information."
McMorris, 34, who is not a teacher, was North Caroline's junior varsity head coach before being named offensive coordinator for the varsity for the 2022 season. When then-head coach James McCormick stepped down after 22 seasons, McMorris was named the school's head varsity coach.
"I'm obviously disheartened and pretty upset about it," McMorris said of the decision. "But I want the kids to go out and win on (Thursday) despite me not being there."
McMorris said junior varsity head coach Heath Wilkins has been promoted to varsity head coach and will be on the sideline Thursday when North Caroline travels to play at James M. Bennett in Salisbury.
"I am genuinely happy for Heath Wilkins, who's taking over," McMorris said. "He's a fantastic coach and literally my number two. He supported me the whole time."
McMorris finishes with a 9-7 career record at North Caroline.
Wilkins, 49, who's been with North Caroline's program for more than five years, was in his third season as junior varsity head coach before his promotion. He played football at Howard High School and then played semi-pro ball for 10 years.
"It's bittersweet," Wilkins said of being named McMorris' successor. "I consider Nic a friend. It's just a bad situation, but I am excited.
"It's a high profile position, and who wouldn't be nervous," Wilkins said of beginning his first varsity head coach job.

title: Peak Tip-Off set for 2 days
author: Bill Haufe

 October 9, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

title: Lions win North despite tie with Bucs
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Lions win North despite tie with Bucs

 October 17, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports

 CENTREVILLE — Queen Anne's County High girls head soccer coach Mike Kern didn't pop out of gear or launch into a tirade.But with his team trailing and doing everything but sticking the ball in the net Wednesday night against Kent Island, Kern was a bit more animated than usual as he pleaded for more.
"I just told them we had to play harder," Kern said. "We were knocking on the doorstep the entire first half. I thought we dominated the game. We had more opportunities to score and we just couldn't get it in the net. I just told them they had to play with a little more heart."
In another physical battle that has become commonplace in this rivalry, Queen Anne's got the equalizing goal it needed, when Shannon Rath buried a penalty kick into the right side of the net in the third minute of the second half in an eventual 1-1 double-overtime tie.
While the Lions and Buccaneers each finished the regular season with identical records — 9-2-1 overall, 6-0-1 North Bayside — Queen Anne's wins the tiebreaker between the two schools based on its 1-0 victory over Kent Island on Sept. 11. Though that first meeting did not count toward the North division, it was the deciding factor since head-to-head competition is the first tiebreaker.
Queen Anne's faces two-time defending conference champion James M. Bennett (12-0) for the Bayside championship on Monday at Snow Hill High School at 6:45 p.m. It will be the fourth consecutive year the Lions and Clippers decide the conference championship. Bennett beat Queen Anne's, 3-0, on Sept. 30 in Centreville.
"I thought Olivia (Ryan) played her best game of the season," Kern said of Wednesday's clash with Kent Island. "So I think we're starting to peak a little bit. We're pretty confident. I think going against (head coach) Ed O'Leary's (Bennett) team, they know us well, we know them well. I think it's going to be a good battle.
"I think this is one of the more talented teams we've ever had," Kern continued. "I mean we can play with anybody as far from 18 to 18. We've struggled to get the ball in the back of the net against these tougher teams. But we can defend. Bennett when we played them last time, we lost 3-0, but the score didn't depict the game. We lost on the scoreboard. But we got to get the ball in the back of the net."
Queen Anne's had three direct kicks and three corner kicks in the first 17 minutes against the Bucs, but could not beat Kent Island keeper Taylor Ritz. Then with 15 minutes left in the half, Buccaneers speedster Abbie Mahaffey — with Queen Anne's Rath trying to shield her from the ball and Lions keeper Bea Holthaus moving toward the ball from the opposite direction — managed to chip a shot that floated over Holthaus for a 1-0 Kent Island lead.
"I think it was just a miscommunication," Kern said of the play. "Shannon running toward her shielding the ball, and Bea coming out. And I think Abbie just made a good play to poke a foot in there and poke it around her. It was just communication."
Kent Island, which stretched its unbeaten streak to nine games after a 1-2 start to the season, held that lead into halftime, despite the Lions swarming near the goal with less than 2 minutes left in the first half in a bid for the tying goal and Ritz away from the net. But the Bucs defense denied Queen Anne's, carrying the 1-0 lead into the break.
The Lions put immediate pressure on Kent Island early in the second half, sending a header over the crossbar. Then with almost 3 minutes elapsed, Kara Ringold was fouled just inside the box, setting up Rath, who roped a shot into the right side past Ritz's dive.
Two yellow cards against the Bucs gave Queen Anne's two more direct-kick chances, but the first sailed wide right and the second was stopped by Ritz.
The Lions came within inches of taking the lead when a shot hit under the crossbar and fell in front of the goal with 9:20 remaining in regulation.

 Giving skaters of all ages a local place to safely hone their skills, Queen Anne's County welcomed a ribbon cutting of Terrapin Skate Park in Stevensville Oct. 18.Complete with quarterpipes, ramps, rails, hubba ledges and more, Terrapin Skate Park is crafted to suit all level of skaters stands as the county's first permanent skatepark, according to Queen Anne's County Parks and Recreation Director Steve Chandlee.
Over two decades ago the parks department established a makeshift skating area but it was hidden away and not utilized well, he said.
Utilizing county owned property, an important aspect of the Terrapin Skate Park project was insuring it was in a visible location, Chandlee said.
In 2022, youths were instrumental in voicing a need to the commissioners and the Parks Advisory Board, including Kent Island High Schooler Dylan Cannon and Violet Baudean, who was a then seventh grader, created a petition highlighting the need for a skatepark.
"We knew upfront this was a great project," Chandlee said.
Now a Kent Island High School sophomore, Baudean is excited to share a love of skating with the community.
Public skateparks highlight a sense of community and offer an outlet for all ages, especially for those who don't drive, according to Baudean.
"There's something here for all skill levels, " she said.
Baudean credited county officials for their support of the project.
While skating is not a team sport, the skating community is very welcoming, always encouraging each other, Chandlee and Baudean said.
"It is a team of support for individuals," Chandlee said.
Funding for the park was made possible through a grant with the Department of Natural Resources Local Parks and Playground Infrastructure, he said.
Breaking ground in April, 12 weeks of construction opened the park to the public in June before stormwater management and tree planting completion officially welcomed the park, according to Chandlee.
More improvements are on the horizon for the park, including bleachers thanks to PRS Guitars and a restroom, he said.
The park has already become a welcome addition of the community with the hope to reach skaters far and wide.
"No matter what, try skateboarding," Baudean said.
Terrapin Skate Park is open sunrise to sunset and patrons are reminded to be respectful of the site and neighbors.
Cars are permitted in the designated parking area and should not be parked in the cul-de-sac or on the roadway.

title: Warriors use stops from Bowen, and goals from Knox, Motovidlak and Quicke in shootout to reach state final four
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Warriors use stops from Bowen, and goals from Knox, Motovidlak and Quicke in shootout to reach state final four

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports

 EASTON — Easton High head field hockey coach Kim Neff started coaching Taylor Bowen when she was five."I always knew she had the potential," Neff said of Bowen. "She's so athletic. And she's got such a high IQ of the game, that I knew she would be a good goalie. And I used to beg her all the time, 'When you get to high school, will you be my goalie?' And finally in seventh grade she turned to me at a rec game and said, 'I'm going to be your goalie in high school.' And I was like, 'Awesome.'"
That described Bowen's performance beautifully Thursday afternoon. Easton's freshman goalie stopped three of the four Hereford players she faced in the 1v1 shootout, and watched teammates Addie Knox, Myka Motovidlak and Ryann Quicke each score goals, propelling the Warriors to a 1-0 victory over the fifth-seeded Bulls in a Class 2A state quarterfinal.
Fourth-seeded Easton (12-3) advances to next Wednesday's 2A state semifinals, where it will meet top-seeded Manchester Valley (15-0) at Glen Burnie High School at a time yet to be determined.
"I don't have enough words to say about her," Neff said of Bowen. "I have believed in her from Day 1. And she believes in herself. She has confidence. And her skills are just growing and growing. She is determined to get better and better, and she has this year. She's just phenomenal."
On an unseasonably warm Halloween day that took a toll on several players, the Warriors and Bulls (11-4) were scoreless after 60 minutes of regulation and two 10-minute overtimes, pushing the duel into a shootout.
Hereford's Gracie Berquist went first in the shootout, but with Bowen moving toward her, fired a shot wide.
Knox went first for Easton, stepped to the right of Bulls goalie Julia Pfitzinger, and sent a shot into the far left corner for a 1-0 Warriors lead.
Caitlin Meeker beat Bowen on Hereford's second attempt to tie the shootout at 1-all. Motovidlak nudged Easton back in front, dodging left and scoring to make it 2-1.
Kayla Owings pushed the ball to the left post on the Bulls' third attempt, but was denied by a diving Bowen.
"Me and my other goalie Alli (Newnam) have trained all season for the shootouts," Bowen said. "And we both hate diving. So we just want to say thank you to (goalie) coach Claire (Spurry), who has been pushing us all season to dive and it worked out perfect. Couldn't ask for a better time."
Quicke was Easton's next shooter.
"I really was down on myself throughout the whole game," Quicke said. "I was getting really frustrated. And my team had told me that this is our only chance right here. 'Why not us?'"
Pfitzinger knocked the ball away from Quicke initially. But the sophomore quickly regained possession and drove the ball into the back of the goal for a 3-1 Easton edge.
"I got a little scared when she cleared it," Quicke said. "But I turned around, and I shot and hoped for it to go in."
Bowen then made a leg save on a shot by Hereford's last hope, Lauren Mathews, then watched the rebound roll out of bounds.
"That was very exciting," Bowen said of her final stop. "I was off my angle, but it all works out. So exciting. Final four."
But before the Warriors launched into a full-blown celebration, they waited for game officials to confirm the game was complete, with Hereford having shot four times and with no chance to tie. Once Easton players got the official stamp on their victory, they stampeded toward their goalie. Leading the charge was Motovidlak, who caught and embraced Bowen in midair. Bowen and Motovidlak were soon taken to ground by an avalanche of teammates.
"Definitely wasn't our best game," Neff said. "I was a little frustrated with them in the first couple quarters. We just weren't playing as a team. But somehow they pulled it off."

title: Lions prepare for first state semifinal since 2004
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Lions prepare for first state semifinal since 2004

 November 5, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 618
 Words 

 Read News Document

 Lexi Kern was going to get a turn regardless."The whole team knows Lexi does well with PKs," Queen Anne's County High girls head soccer coach Mike Kern said of his daughter.
Coach Kern sent his 11 players onto the field for a shootout to decide last Friday's Class 2A state quarterfinal against Wilde Lake, but noticed his third and fourth shooters had bumped themselves further back in the lineup. After Shannon Rath and Morgan Scott each buried their PKs, Kern watched his daughter move into the third spot and step behind the ball.
"She said, 'OK, I'll go,'" the coach said.
Like Rath and Scott, Lexi Kern parked her PK in the right corner, then watched Wilde Lake's third attempt miss the mark, sealing a 1-0 victory that gave the Lions their first state semifinal berth since 2004.
Second-seeded Queen Anne's (12-3-1) advances to Saturday's 2A state semifinals, where it will meet No. 3 seed Century (12-2-1) at 2:30 p.m. at Kent Island High School in Stevensville.
"That was kind of a cool moment for me," Mike Kern said of Lexi's PK. "Nobody else wanted it, which is the crazy part. Lexi is usually four or five or six (in the PK lineup). They just did not want to take it."
The Lions followed a familiar pattern against the seventh-seeded Wildecats (7-6-3), dominating play without benefit of a goal — though one score was negated by a questionable offsides call.
After two overtime periods, the game moved into penalty kicks.
"I was surprised how calm I was," said Mike Kern, who noted an eerie quiet fell over Lions Stadium during the shootout. "It was like golf. You could hear a pin drop. Both teams. After they made them they cheered. But it was quiet as could be. I had never experienced anything like that."
Queen Anne's went first, with Rath driving a shot into the right side of the net. Wilde Lake's first PK sailed over the crossbar.
Celebrating her 18th birthday, Scott deposited her PK in nearly the exact same spot at Rath's shot. The Wildecats' second attempt went wide. Lexi Kern promptly booted her shot into the right corner for a 3-0 lead. Wilde Lake's third — and final chance — again went well over the head of Lions keeper Bea Holthaus and the crossbar, clinching the victory.
This is the Lions' third trip to the state semifinals under their 24-year head coach. Queen Anne's last reached the state semis as a 1A school in 2004, when it lost in the closing minute of double overtime to Tuscarora. Queen Anne's also reached the state semifinals in 2003, outlasting Oakland Mills in an 11-man shootout before falling in the state final.
Kern and longtime assistant Jeff Anthony have built solid teams in the past, but often were eliminated by 2A powers Fallston and Bel Air.
But this season, Kern thought he had the goods to make a return trip to the final four.
"I really thought this team had the chance to get there," Kern said. "I think they're competitors. They love to compete. Even at practice with each other, they don't like to lose. And I think they accept challenges. They've been together for so long and played together for a long time. And I think they feed off each other. I think that they're competitors is the biggest thing."
Queen Anne's has posted 10 shutouts this season, and now faces a Century program that won the state title just two years ago. Since losing their first two games of the season by a combined score of 7-0, the Knights have gone 12-0-1 and logged 11 shutouts, including 10 straight.
"They very defensive," Kern said of the Knights. "They are very similar to us. I think we've got a legitimate shot."

title: QA’s, Easton hoping for a Shore thing
author: Bill Haufe

 They battled each other in one of the season's more memorable duels, playing 80 scoreless minutes before settling things in 1v1s.That was Oct. 1, when Queen Anne's County High's field hockey team outlasted Easton in a shootout, part of a 14-game Lions' unbeaten streak.
The Warriors have not lost since that clash, reeling off eight straight victories.
Wednesday, 36 days later after that marathon, Queen Anne's and Easton prepare to play in the Class 2A state semifinals at Glen Burnie High School, not against each other, but hoping to possibly create the first all-Eastern Shore state final since 1997.
"How great would it be?" Queen Anne's longtime head coach Shana Corder asked rhetorically. "I am rooting for Easton and Queen Anne's to win this one. I think that would be an awesome setup."
Warrior head coach Kim Neff seconded that notion.
"That would be so wild," Neff said of an all-Shore final that hasn't happened since Pocomoke defeated Kent County in the 1997 Class 1A championship. "That would be so cool."
Of course, Corder and Neff each know that dream match doesn't happen unless their respective teams get past a pair of unbeatens tonight.
Third-seeded Queen Anne's (13-1-1) goes first, when it plays three-time defending state champion and No. 2 seed Glenelg (15-0) at 5:30 p.m. Fourth-seeded Easton (12-3) follows in a meeting with No. 1 seed Manchester Valley (15-0) at 7:30 p.m.
"OK. So we're not undefeated," Corder said. "We're the underdog."
The Lions may have thought they would be wearing that underdog tag through at least part of this season after graduating a number of standouts off last year's 15-1 team that posted 14 shutouts and reached the state semifinals. Corder honestly thought this would be a rebuild season, since the entire defense from a year ago — with the exception of goalie Cassidy Alexander — was gone.
But after a season-opening loss at Pocomoke, Corder changed her position.
"I think they felt, 'Oh, we're not going to be as good,'" Corder said. "'We are not as good as this team.' But I was like, 'We are as good. You can't set yourself up to think you're a failure.' I think losing that game was the best blessing we've gotten all year.
"I saw their faces and they weren't used to losing, all my returners," Corder continued. "And I felt like they didn't like to lose. So I thought that gave them the drive to want to win. I felt that was our turning point."
Since then the Lions, behind their one-two goalie punch of Caroline Kimball and Alexander, and a rebuilt defense, have gone unbeaten, which included winning their second straight Bayside Conference and regional championships — a first in program history — and recording 11 shutouts.
"I feel every team we play has given us their best game because we did so well (last year)," Corder said. "They understand pressure. They've been here before. All the returners know what this feels like. Hopefully they already felt the pressure. We've had 1v1 games, overtime, blah, blah, blah. I'm just hoping they are able to rise to the occasion Wednesday."
Though Easton didn't have a 2023 season that compared to Queen Anne's, Neff was filled with optimism at the outset of this season.
"I knew we were capable of getting this far," Neff said. "A lot of these girls I've coached since they were in kindergarten, and I know their potential. It was the most athletic group that I have seen (during preseason tryouts). I think them playing some travel ball together and being on rec teams together, they know each other well, which helps."
But Easton's record was sitting at 4-3 after the 1v1 loss to Queen Anne's. The Warriors moved to 5-3 with a shutout of Kent County.
Then came a 3-2 overtime victory over Pocomoke.
"We have a long history with Pocomoke," Neff said. "And Pocomoke tends to get the victories. So I think that game, and going into overtime, and doing what they did really solidified them. Like I knew and I had the confidence in them. But I think it solidified the confidence in them, like, 'We can do this.'"
Since that victory, Easton has defeated perennial Bayside heavyweight Kent Island 1-0 in overtime. The Warriors defeated Parkside 2-1 in overtime in a 2A East Region II semifinal, then beat Stephen Decatur 2-1 with 11 seconds remaining in regulation in the region final. Easton continued its trend for the dramatic last Thursday, defeating Hereford in a 1v1 in a state quarterfinal, placing the Warriors in the state semifinals for the first time since 2021.
"I told them, 'You've earned your spot there,'" Neff said. "'We're all good teams. We made it to the top four. We're not looking at records because every day's a clean slate for every team. We haven't seen them (Manchester Valley). They haven't seen us. And so we're going in and we're playing our game. They're ready."

title: Lions, Warriors fall shy in final bids
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Lions, Warriors fall shy in final bids

 November 7, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 807
 Words 

 Read News Document

 GLEN BURNIE — Glenelg High head field hockey coach Martie Dyer didn't panic when her team fell behind for the first time all year."I was disappointed obviously," Dyer said when Queen Anne's County took a lead less than 5 minutes into Wednesday's Class 2A state semifinal. "But I didn't go, 'Oh, no. This is going to be terrible.'"
Dyer admitted she was worried though with the Gladiators holding just a one-goal lead midway through the fourth quarter.
"I kept telling the girls, 'I need an insurance goal,'" Dyer said. "'I can't have the game be 2-1 and then risk a breakaway and tie game.' I got a little emotional at the fourth quarter and said, 'You can't lose this game.' I just started to choke up. And they said, 'We got you coach Marti.'"
It took a few minutes to ease Dyer's tension, but Brinkley Eyre's penalty stroke with 4:15 remaining provided the cushion the Gladiators' head coach was looking for in an eventual 4-1 victory over the Lions at Glen Burnie High School's Pop Whayland Stadium.
Second-seeded Glenelg (16-0) will bid for a fourth consecutive Class 2A state title Saturday at 11 a.m., when it faces top-seeded Manchester Valley (16-0) in the championship game at Stevenson University's Mustang Stadium.
"I felt we played a great 50 minutes of field hockey," said Queen Anne's head coach Shana Corder, whose team had not given up multiple goals in a game since 2022. "We had 'em 2-1. We scored first, got the momentum going. They answered back a little bit later and scored. I mean they are a fabulous team. And they are so fast. I just thought my team rose to the occasion."
Queen Anne's Aly Edwards may have shaken the Gladiator faithful when she knocked the ball past Glenelg goalie Trinity Shackelford (seven saves) 4:15 into the game for a 1-0 Lions lead.
"I saw how much we were dominating and they just happened to get us on a fastbreak," Dyer said. "And that happens. And then we put that other goal in and I thought, 'OK, it's back to zero-zero.' I purposely don't try to make a big deal about that so they don't get it in their head like, 'Oh, my gosh.'"
A little over 3 minutes later, Queen Anne's goalie Cassidy Alexander was guarding the right post on a corner when Glenelg's Meghan Walker got behind her and tapped in the equalizer for a 1-1 tie.
The Gladiators then took a lead they never relinquished at 2-1 when Eyre — the talented senior center midfielder who has netted 57 goals and 21 assists this season and his headed to the University of Maryland — set up Lexi Winters' goal with 10:50 left in the first half.
But Glenelg could not extend that lead despite earning three more penalty corners over the final 3:42 of the first half against Queen Anne's Caroline Kimball, who played the second and fourth quarters, and together with Alexander made 14 saves.
"I thought they did a nice job," Dyer said of the Lions' penalty-corner defense. "They came out very fast on corners. Their fly, as it's called, came out very fast on Brinkley. Yeah, that was somewhat of a factor."
Kimball made a save 34 seconds before halftime on the Gladiators' seventh corner of the first half. Glenelg crossed a pass through the crease with 7:30 left in the third quarter but had no one positioned at the far post.
Queen Anne's (13-2-1) fired wide on a corner with 5:48 left in the third, then had another shot stopped by Shackelford a few seconds later.
Alexander made a diving stop to keep the Lions' deficit at one with 1:49 to go in the third. Queen Anne's Haley Cole then sent a hard drive from the right side that missed connecting with two teammates stationed at the far post with under a minute remaining in the third.
Kimball made a save on another Glenelg corner early in the fourth, then stopped a sweeping backhand from Eyre with 7:44 remaining.
"They did amazing," Corder said of Alexander and Kimball. "They're two phenomenal goalies."
Eyre was then fouled with 4:15 remaining setting up her stroke. Alexander returned for the stroke and watched as Eyre snapped a shot into the upper left corner for a 3-1 edge.
"We were in the game until the stroke call," Corder said. "That happens. Nothing you can really do about that. And then that put it at 3-1 and kind of seals the deal."
Glenelg, which had won its region final and state quarterfinal by a combined score of 20-1, padded its lead with under 2 minutes left, when Kimball made another big save on Eyre, only to have Lakshmi Almili feed Walker for her second goal and a 4-1 final.
"They got that late goal with two minutes to go or whatever, but I'm super proud," Corder said. "I thought my girls played really well."

title: Top-sdded Mavs oust Easton
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Top-sdded Mavs oust Easton

 November 7, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 650
 Words 

 Read News Document

 GLEN BURNIE — It had found multiple ways to win since early October.Easton High's field hockey team had won in overtime and double overtime. It had won with 11 seconds remaining in regulation. It had won on a penalty stroke and in a 1v1. And it continued to find paths to victory no matter how big the game.
But Wednesday night against top-seeded Manchester Valley, the Warrior offense rarely found its way into the circle and had its storybook season ended in a 3-0 loss to the Mavericks in a Class 2A state semifinal at Glen Burnie High School's Pop Whayland Stadium.
Manchester Valley (16-0) advances to Saturday's 11 a.m. Class 2A state championship game where it will meet three-time defending state champion Glenelg (16-0) at Stevenson University's Mustang Stadium.
"I'm so proud of them," said Easton head coach Kim Neff, whose team had its eight-game win streak ended, finishing the year at 12-4. "Taylor Bowen again had so many shots on her that she was able to save. They battled many corners clear. It was a defensive-heavy game and they handled it very well."
Indeed, the Mavericks, who had blanked their previous three playoff opponents by a combined 27-0, were held to their lowest goal total of the postseason.
"Their whole team, they played hard," Manchester Valley head coach Denean Koontz said. "They did a very nice job of doubling us. They took us out of our game plan a little bit. They stepped to the ball very well. Defensively, they were on us everywhere. They did a very nice job of smothering the ball and smothering our players."
The Mavericks finished with 11 corners before Easton earned its first with only 1 minute, 26 seconds remaining in the game.
By then the No. 1 seed had already built a three-goal cushion that was started off a pair of first-quarter corners.
Bowen, Easton's freshman goalie, and her defense weathered Manchester Valley's first two corners in the opening 5 minutes. The Mavericks were awarded their third corner less than 3 minutes later and converted, as Lily Brookhart scored off Shelby Wurzburger's assist for a 1-0 lead.
Manchester Valley earned its fifth corner with 13 seconds remaining in the first quarter, and again capitalized, with Allie Largent setting up Brookhart's second goal with no time showing on the clock.
"They were aggressive," Neff said of Manchester Valley, which held Easton scoreless for the first time since a 1v1 loss to Queen Anne's on Oct. 1. "And their stick skills were incredible."
Bowen made a save on the Mavs' first corner of the second period, and watched her teammates foil a second corner near the end of the period.
But Easton generated little offense, the long rushes downfield by Olivia Orrell and Addie Knox were often and quickly stopped well short of the circle.
"I do feel like my girls held their own," Neff said. "And I think this is where it really comes into play not having a turf field, and not being able to practice on a turf field, and play on a turf field. It's hard to keep up with the competition. Their whole team was just fast."
Manchester Valley picked up three more corner chances in the third, but could not add to its lead as Bowen registered two more saves on corners.
"Our defense, our middies, they all stepped up," Neff said. "I will say I feel like each quarter we came out a little more aggressive cutting to the ball better. I feel if we had one more quarter you might have seen maybe a goal."
Manchester Valley put away one more goal with only 4 seconds left on the third-quarter clock, when Carroll County scoring leader Amanda Herrold scored on a breakaway.
Though they continued battling, the Warriors mounted few threats and got their first corners in succession with 1:26 left, when Mavericks' goalie Makayla Shoaf registered her lone save.
"They played hard," Koontz said of Easton. "They did a great job."

title: Bucs can't sustain momentum against Wildcats
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Bucs can't sustain momentum against Wildcats

 November 10, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 693
 Words 

 Read News Document

 STEVENSVILLE — It had cut its deficit in half, rallying and grinding to a Game 3 victory.Playing on its home floor, Kent Island High's volleyball team had momentum, and may have even felt it had gained a bit of traction. But that momentum was quickly extinguished Saturday, as Williamsport built an early Game 4 lead it steadily expanded on the way to sealing a 25-16, 25-15, 23-25, 25-9 victory over the Buccaneers in a Class 2A state quarterfinal.
No. 7 Williamsport (12-5) advances to Tuesday's 2A state semifinals at Watkins Mill High School in Gaithersburg, where it will face third-seeded Calvert (15-2) at 5 p.m.
"That third set, just getting that little bit of momentum, and placing the ball and playing a little bit smarter, that's what won us the victory there," Kent Island first-year head coach Brittney Guy said.
Despite pulling within 2-1, Guy reminded her team, "That set's over with. You've got to move on. We've got to play composed and play our game."
But the Wildcats recaptured momentum early in the fourth set, getting a side out before Kennedi Lawhorne reeled off three consecutive service points for a 4-0 lead.
"We kind of got stump on our serve-receive," Williamsport head coach Karen Hampton said of the Game 3 loss. "They were serving us really tough. So once we were able to kind of fix that we kind of got back on track.
"We definitely wanted to start out with a lead," Hampton said of Game 4. "We were receiving serve, so our goal was to side out on that very first ball so we could get it and try to get the momentum early. And we were able to do that."
The second-seeded Bucs (15-3) stopped that early run via Macayla Kirk's kill to make it 4-1. An errant Kent Island return made it 8-3, bringing Skylar Norris to the service line, where she remained until delivering an ace that punctuated a 10-point service streak for an 18-3 Williamsport lead.
"Coming into the fourth set, energy was low," Guy said. "Communication was low on the court. We came back a little bit. They dug deep, but it was just a little too late in that fourth set."
Kent Island never had back-to-back service points in Game 4, as Norris' kill on the final point sealed the 25-9 victory and the Wildcats' 26th trip to the state semifinals.
"We had a bus ride; a long ride," Hampton said of her team's trip from Washington County. "So we had to kind of get loose a little bit. But once we found our groove and we found our rhythm, I felt like we were able to execute what we needed to."
That was apparent in Game 1, as a game-opening side out, coupled with Alaina Dlabich's four-point service run, staked Kent Island to 5-0 lead. The Bucs clung to their lead until a net return on a serve by Williamsport's Elizabeth Warren forged the game's first tie at 14-all. It remained tight until the Bucs struggled returning Norris' serve, helping the Wildcats score the final nine points of Game 1 for a 1-0 lead.
Game 2 was also tight early, but again Williamsport closed strong, netting the last 10 points for a 25-15 win.
"We missed a few more serves than we normally do," Guy said. "Just the technique-wise, when you come into games like this with teams like this, everything technically has to be right. You got to be ready in the right defensive spot. I don't think we completely gave it to them, but we could have played a little bit more diligent ball. The opposing team, they played very smart."
Warren's five-point service run helped the Wildcats to a 7-2 lead in Game 3. But in a game that included seven ties — the last at 20-20 — Kent Island took a 21-20 lead on Dlabich's block. Williamsport hit an errant return on a Gianna King serve to make it 22-20. Kirk's block and a returning error moved the Bucs to a 24-21 lead. Williamsport pulled within 24-23 before Kirk drove a winner into a vacant left corner for a 25-23 Bucs win — giving Williamsport its first loss in three postseason matches.

title: North Dorchester's deepest run ends
author: Bill Haufe
content:
North Dorchester's deepest run ends

 November 13, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 557
 Words 

 Read News Document

 GAMBRILLS — Carol Hubbard knows it takes time to build programs.In the spring of 2023, Hubbard guided North Dorchester High's softball team to its first Class 1A state championship.
Hubbard guided the Eagles to yet another first this year, leading the volleyball team to a Class 1A state semifinal berth for the first time in the program's 11-year history.
That bid for a state crown ended though Tuesday night at Arundel High School, as second-seeded Boonsboro swept No. 6 seed North Dorchester, 25-12, 25-6, 25-13 in that 1A state semifinal.
The Warriors (16-3) will play fifth-seeded Clear Spring (14-5) at noon on Saturday for the 1A state championship at Harford Community College's APG Federal Credit Union Arena.
"It was a huge accomplishment for them to get to this point," said Hubbard, whose team had a five-match win streak ended, finishing the year 12-7. "This is the farthest that any team has gone in our program."
North Dorchester scored the first point of the night, and stayed within two to three points of the Warriors early. But a four-point service run from Larissa Blair, that included a pair of kills from Rosslyn Briggs, helped give Boonsboro separation in Game 1 at 15-6. Another Briggs kill and an ace from Aly Phillips extended the Warriors lead to 19-8. Back-to-back errant returns by the Eagles closed the 25-12 set.
"Our game plan coming in is to always serve tough," Boonsboro seven-year head coach Shelby Wallace said. "But we had a few select styles of serve that we wanted to execute today and I think we did that. Mostly the deep float and some short serves where appropriate."
Those service combinations fueled Boonsboro's most dominant set of the match, as Devin Glines served 10 straight points before Blair reeled off a five-point run in Game 2.
"Serve-receive struggled," Hubbard said of her team. "And then when we did get a decent pass we weren't able to capitalize on it on the front row. So it was just kind of a snowball. I think the front row was getting frustrated with the back row some, and then the back row would finally get (the ball) up and they were getting frustrated with the front row."
A service error and back-to-back points off Katelyn Hopkins' serve gave North Dorchester a 4-3 edge in Game 3. Boonsboro rallied to a 9-5 lead. Brooke Outten answered, coupling a kill with consecutive aces to draw the Eagles within 9-8.
But Boonsboro steadily began widening its lead. A Warrior kill and two return errors bumped the gap to 13-8. Brooke Iager then delivered back-to-back aces to open a five-point service spree that gave Boonsboro a 19-9 lead. North Dorchester kept its deficit under 10 before Anna Jackson's kill and two errant returns capped the 25-13 Game 3 win.
"The third set early on we had a little run there and evened it up," Hubbard said. "I tip my hat to them. They are a strong team.
"As far as an all-around balanced team, I would say they're the best that we've seen," Hubbard added of Boonsboro, which advanced to its first state final since 2007. "They didn't have a weak spot. They were strong all the way around. You play some teams and they have a really strong outside hitter, or a really strong middle hitter. I would say they were as well-rounded a team as we've faced."

title: Chesapeake passes early eye test
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Chesapeake passes early eye test

 November 20, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 792
 Words 

 Read News Document

 WYE MILLS — Chesapeake College men's head basketball coach Andrew Sachs knew his team was going to lose at some point this season.The Skipjacks did that for only the first time this young season on Tuesday night, 92-88, in overtime to visiting Montgomery College.
But Chesapeake has also won — all four of its games prior to Tuesday — and Sachs has liked what he's seen.
"They like being around each other," said Sachs, now in his fifth season at Wye Mills. "There's no selfishness, which again at this level, you get that at times.
"And look how many guys are averaging double figures (in scoring) for us," continued Sachs, who has four after five games. "That's always a telltale sign. It should be four, almost six. That's what you want. All my good teams at every level that I've been at, we've always had four or five guys averaging in double figures. Always."
Leading that foursome is freshman point guard La'Shaun Moody (19.2 points per game), who helped lead Cambridge-South Dorchester High to the Class 1A state final last season. He is followed by sophomore backcourt mates Brandon Hooks (14.8 ppg.) and Eli Credle (12.2 ppg.), and sophomore forward Willie Jones (15.0), who is yanking down an average of nine rebounds a contest.
Not far behind them are sophomore guard Ashton Pratt (9.3) and freshman guard Brayden Smith (8.0), who helped Saints Peter and Paul win the Maryland Interscholastic Athletic Association C Conference championship earlier this year.
"Winning helps everybody," Sachs said as his team was wrapping up practice Friday morning. "And I think another thing is they see themselves getting better. That's a big thing. Because if they didn't see that, then you would hear grumbling. But they can see themselves getting better."
And the Skipjacks have the potential to get even better as soon as sophomore forwards Shaft Clark and DaQuan Johnson get on the court. Chesapeake's frontcourt is currently a rotation of the 6-foot-5 Jones, 6-4 Josh Rivers, who returns from last season, and freshmen Kionne Lang (6-6) and Narayan Thomas (6-5).
"I still think we have a big learning curve," Sachs said. "But we've really played some pretty good teams."
Chesapeake opened with an 83-66 victory over Fayetteville Technical Community College (N.C.) before a road win at Louisburg Community College (N.C.). The Skipjacks drained a school single-game record 21 3-pointers in a 41-point rout of Pennsylvania Highlands, then defeated defending Region XIX champion Raritan Valley (N.J.).
"I feel like the starting five we have right now is pretty good all around," said Credle, a member of the 2022-23 Chesapeake team that reached the national tournament, but sat out all last year due to a knee injury. "We have three really good wings. We have Brandon that can shoot the ball really well off the catch. Josh can shoot it well. And we have Willie that can shoot the ball probably the best on our team right now. And we have Kionne, and he's getting better ever day. We just have to keep on building."
Sachs thinks he already has a better-built backcourt than last season, when the Skipjacks finished 14-17. A transfer, Hooks has a quick release and has started strong, and Credle has returned after red-shirting last season.
"A really good player," Sachs said of Credle. "Handles the basketball. Runs the team. We had no point guard last year. And to have two really good ones this year makes a world of difference."
That other point guard is the mercurial Moody, who's "been way more than anyone has asked for," Sachs said. "He's been the energy guy for us. Good on-ball defender. Makes plays. Got a lot of grit. It's been a great start to his career."
Moody led Cambridge-SD to a 25-3 record, its first Bayside Conference championship since 1996 last season, as well as a berth in the Class 1A state final, where the Vikings lost to Edmondson-Westside. And it doesn't appear he's lost an ounce of the intensity he played with throughout his high school career.
"There's some things he needs to learn and he's had a few rough spots," Sachs said of Moody. "But In terms of consistency, no one matches his energy. And everybody gets better when he's on the floor. And that's what a point guard does. Number one job of a point guard is to make the other four guys on the floor better. And both of those guys do that. We did not have that last year."
Depth in the backcourt is provided by sophomores Da'Mir Camper and Joshua DeJesus, and freshman Xavier Buchanan.
"I love the group of kids we have," Sachs said. "They all love each other. They love basketball. Basketball's important to them. Winning's important. I think we can be pretty good. We're just going to try to keep getting better."
