title: Vikings face Fort Hill in quarterfinals instead of title bout
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Vikings face Fort Hill in quarterfinals instead of title bout

 November 21, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 798
 Words 

 Read News Document

 With the exception of a few injuries, and the assorted turnovers and penalties that leave coaches muttering, the season has gone pretty much as planned for Cambridge-South Dorchester High's football team."We had talked all season," first-year Vikings' head coach Rob Burnham said, "about doing the things we're supposed to do, and being successful, and work hard, and improve day after day. Get through the season undefeated. Get the number one overall seed in the (Class) 1A, and then we won't play the Sentinels until we go to Annapolis. Obviously, things changed on that."
Cambridge-SD did go undefeated during the regular season and earned the No. 1 overall seed when the state playoffs were reseeded last week.
As for meeting three-time defending 1A state champion Fort Hill in a potential state-title showdown in Annapolis? Well, that changed when the Sentinels forfeited five regular-season games for using an ineligible player. Fort Hill remained eligible for the postseason though, romped to a pair of regional victories, and come into Friday's 6:30 p.m. state quarterfinal at Cambridge-SD (10-0) as the No. 8 seed at 4-7.
"I met with our guys and said, 'Obviously the circumstances have changed and what we worked hard for isn't necessarily going to be given to us,'" Burnham said. "'We still have to go out and take it. So in order to get what we want we have to beat them. We just have to do it two weeks earlier than we had planned on.'"
A Cambridge-SD assistant last year, Burnham and Fort Hill head coach Zack Alkire agreed this is not the same Sentinels team that routed the Vikings, 38-20, in last year's state semifinals in Cumberland.
"We have a much better shot to run the ball on them this year than last year," Burnham said. "I've coached for 26 years and that was the best high school team I've seen regardless of classification in three different states. They were really good."
But that team that went on to win a third straight state title while extending its winning streak to 21 games, graduated 20 players, and is not as senior heavy this year.
"We play 10 sophomores throughout the course of a game and they've done really well for us," Alkire said. "There's been some growing pains. But the seniors have shown good leadership and gotten those guys to get us to where we are today."
One thing hasn't changed though with the Sentinels.
"Still the same ground-and-pound style of offense," Alkire said. "We try to spread you out when we can, but it's mostly going to be under center, ground and pound."
Leading that rushing attack is senior running back Jabril Daniels, who has toted the ball 156 times for 1,664 yards and 26 touchdowns this season. Braelyn Younger (43-485-9) is also a threat. And though senior quarterback Nash Cassell, who has completed 13 of 27 passes for 276 yards and six touchdowns, isn't a huge running threat, Alkire said he "does a great job of getting the ball where it needs to be."
That offense faces one of the Bayside Conference's quickest defenses.
"They're very aggressive defensively; try to cause problems in your backfield," Alkire said of Cambridge-SD.
But Burnham knows the unit he's called the backbone of his team since August, faces perhaps its biggest test of the season.
"Fort Hill football is Fort Hill football," Burnham said. "They play physical. They play fast. They do multiple things offensively. They run the ball consistently with multiple backs. We have to contain their run, limit their explosive plays on defense."
Cambridge-SD also possesses big-play talent, with senior quarterback Anthony Hughes and senior running back Sterling Perkins Jr., who has gained over a 1,000 yards this season.
"Offensively, we need to protect the football and then be opportunistic and make plays when we can," Burnham said.
Though the Sentinels have usually been at home during the past three postseasons, Alkire said his team has adapted to playing on the road after the ineligibility ruling.
"Just a matter of getting the kids in the mindset to be able to go on the road and endure some of the longer road trips, and experience some of the things that opposing teams have had to experience against us," Alkire said. "It's been a transition but the kids have accepted it and they moved on."
And though its date with Fort Hill has come two weeks earlier than expected, Burnham thinks the Vikings are ready.
"I think our kids are excited about an opportunity to prove ourself on a big stage against a quality opponent," Burnham said. "In order to get where we want to be we have to beat them. To coin the phrase, 'To be the man you've got to beat the man.' They've been the man the last three years and we want to take it. So we have to win. That's how it is."

title: Kerns, Queen Anne's thinking they have the goods for another long postseason run.
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Kerns, Queen Anne's thinking they have the goods for another long postseason run.

 December 4, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 2164
 Words 

 Read News Document

 It wasn't a prediction.It was just something Mike Kern believed.
"If we can get out of the region, I think we have a good shot at states," Kern said of Queen Anne's County High's girls soccer team.
That was at the outset of the season. The Lions did get out of the region, then went on to become the first Bayside Conference school ever to win a girls state soccer championship.
Now, as the girls basketball season approaches tip-off, Kern again strongly believes if Queen Anne's can get out of its region, it has a chance to do well at the state level.
"We're very multi-dimensional," Kern said. "All of our guards can penetrate and shoot. And then our post players are very dangerous inside. They move well. They're very athletic. So I think the sky's the limit for them. The biggest thing is play as a team. We learned that in soccer. If we play as a team and aren't selfish, and do the little things, I think we can do really well."
Getting out of the Class 2A East Region II could prove more difficult than in soccer. Kent Island still has Sydney Riska and Lacey Dauses. Wicomico returns the bulk of the team that handed the Lions their only three losses last season, including bouts for the Bayside Conference and 2A East Region II championships. And Parkside has improved.
But this Queen Anne's team is different.
Not only does Kern return the majority of a team that went 20-3 and won the North Bayside championship, he welcomes two additions who have the potential to be impact players in juniors Damya Henry, a transfer from Cambridge-South Dorchester, and Cheyanne Hollis — daughter of Queen Anne's boys head coach Jeff Hollis — who has been sidelined by injury the past two seasons.
"With our core coming back, plus those additions, I think we stand a good chance of challenging them this year," Kern said of Wicomico. "Damya gives us that defensive pressure. She reads well. Anticipates well. And she's quick. So she definitely helps on the defensive end.
"And Chayenne, she's a true post player; and that will free up Bea (Holthaus) and Lucy (Taylor) a little bit having her in there," Kern continued.
Then there's the core group. Seniors RJ Ensor and Lucy Taylor return along with sophomores Laila Coles, Kariana Hickson, and Holthaus, the 2023 North Bayside Player of the Year.
"The thing about our team right now, I feel like we can score so many different ways," Kern said. "We have pretty good shooters. We can get the ball inside. We can drive. We're a very multi-dimensional team. And Bea herself is very multi-dimensional. She can play outside, go inside. She can drive.
"I'm not worried about us being able to score this year," Kern added. "My biggest focus so far is making sure we play good defense. One of the things that we've done well over the years is we've been a really good defensive team. And I feel like we have so much energy on the offense, that we kind of rest on the defense. And we can't do that with good teams. So we have to play up-tempo defense the entire game."
Kent Island remains Queen Anne's biggest challenger, though Cambridge-SD, with the senior core of Le'Asia Todd, Destiny Johnson and Tejanae Ballin have the potential to give Queen Anne's a battle.
Here's a look at this season's teams.
CAMBRIDGE-SD
Head Coach: Shamya Johnson.
Who's Where: Le'Asia Todd (Sr., C); Destiny Johnson (Sr., G); Tejanae Ballin (Sr., PG); AzEyera Johnson (Sr., F); Skyla Ali (So., F); Jade Ballin (So., F); JaNaya Stanley (Jr., G); Tonyia Brooks (Sr., G); Aamiyah Wilcox (Sr., C); Neveah Adams (Fr., G); Montiasha Jackson (So., G); Amari Winters (Fr., F/C); Kennedy Bourne (So., F); Kamryn Bourne (So., F); D'Asia Mack (So., G).
Outlook: Todd can reach 1,000 career points in Thursday's opener against Crisfield, and together with Destiny Johnson and Tejanae Ballin makes the Vikings a favorite in 1A East Region II.
And though Coach Johnson thinks Cambridge-SD can again reach the 1A state quarterfinals, one of her biggest challenges is keeping her team's intensity and discipline up from start to finish.
"That was the conversation we had tonight,' Coach Johnson said Tuesday in a phone interview. "'You all got it. You've got the pieces. But you all don't have the discipline. And that's the difference.'"
Johnson also knows her team needs to play great transition defense and create points off turnovers if it hopes to challenge Queen Anne's and Kent Island.
COL. RICHARDSON
Head Coach: Tom Corsey.
Who's Where: Jaz Jackson (Jr., G); Monae Ross (Sr., C); Selina Austriville (So., F); Tybria Williams (Sr., G); Ella Downie (So., F); Angelina Algre (Fr., C).
Outlook: Corsey thinks the 6-foot-5 Algre can develop into an inside force.
"She's a work in progress," Corsey said. "She's a presence. She's learning, but I'm going to get her there."
This is one of the younger teams Corsey's coached, but the goal is another 10-win season with eyes on upsetting a 2A school.
EASTON
Head Coach: Lesley Staehli.
Who's Where: Sam Murphy (Sr., G); Serenity Velez (Jr., G); Maia Bailey (Fr., G); Ki'Mauri Lewis (So., G); Jordyn Wilson-Colbert (So., F/C); Myles Booker (Sr., F/C); Dakota Dietrich (Sr., G); Addison Knox (So., G/F); Stella Kabler (Jr., G); Taylor Bowen (Fr., F/C); Addison Chandler (Sr., G/F).
Outlook: The Warriors are an interesting mix.
Velez returns as one of the team's top scorers, and Murphy has transferred from Saints Peter and Paul.
"She is one of the scrappiest people I have ever played against the last four years that I've been coaching defense wise," Staehli said of Murphy. "Now it's awesome to have her with us because she barely comes out."
Bailey, daughter of Marty Bailey, who has come over from the boys team to be an assistant, could be one of the Bayside's top newcomers. And then there is a list of talent that includes Knox, Kabler and Bowen, who helped the Warriors reach the state field hockey semifinals this past season, and Chandler, a force on the Easton soccer team.
"We're going to be fast," Staehli said. "Everybody has talent. I think we're going to shock a lot of people this year with the fact (they're) not expecting a lot of athletic people to come back into the program with us having no jayvee last year. There's certain teams we'll struggle with, but I think we're going to be pretty good."
KENT COUNTY
Head Coach: Tyray Johnson.
Who's Where: Kate Cannon (Sr., C); Talicia Wright (So., PG); Jane Cleary (So., F); Love Jackson (Jr., SF); Kaliyah Smith (Sr., SF); Ariyana Green (So., SF); Saniyah Jones (So., C); Tameeia Savage (Jr., SF); Juliette Camilli (Jr., SG); Sanorra Parker (Fr., SG); Abigael Lachance (Sr., SF); Emerence Boutaud (Jr., PF).
Outlook: Johnson begins his fourth season with the biggest roster he's ever had at Kent with 12. Though still young, experience was gained last year, especially with Wright, who returns at point guard.
"We turned the ball over a lot last year," Johnson said. "She (Wright) stepped up toward the end of the season. So a lot of the mistakes she made early on we won't really have them this year. So it's going to be less turnovers for us."
Speed and defense will be critical if the undersized Trojans are to improve on last season's five-win mark.
KENT ISLAND
Head Coach: Dave Plumer.
Who's Where: Sydney Riska (Sr., F); Lacey Dauses (Jr., G); Abigail Staton (Sr., PG); Ellie Burnside (Sr., G); Machaela Thomas (So., C); Avery Eaton (Sr., G)
Outlook: Lilli Dauses graduated and Makayla Kropfelder transferred to Broadneck. But don't expect the Bucs to fall far from the top.
The smooth-playing Riska was a double-double machine last season, and Lacey Dauses gained confidence with her ability to attack the rim and draw contact. Add Thomas, a 6-foot-2 center, who could create problems for opponents, and Burnside, the first player off the bench from last season.
"I think Lacey had grown as a player and in size," Plumer said. "Obviously Sydney had a big year last year, and now adding another 6-2 center to play along side of her is going to benefit her as well. Who are you going to guard? Machaela's got great footwork. She just needs playing time to get better.
"I think we got to run," Plumer continued. "I mean we're guard heavy. We do have a big player inside but I think we're going to be a running team. We just got to play. There's talent there. It's going to take them a month or two to get them up to speed. But they can play."
NORTH CAROLINE
Head Coach: AJ Jackson.
Who's Where: Taryn Brandt (Sr., G); Jasiyah Henry (Sr., G); Emma Keating (Sr., F); Ashley Kercheval (Sr., F); Megan Rogers (Sr., G); Kaitlyn Thompson (Sr., C); Sarah Brown (Sr., G); MyKira Allen (Jr., F); Yariah Dowell (Jr., G); Irma Sanchez (Jr., G); Nevaeh Irby (So., G).
Outlook: The Bulldogs lost the majority of their scoring from last season with the graduation of Precious Phillips, Chloe Escoe, Ashleigh Lawry and first-team all-North Bayside pick Selaya Garrison.
Jackson will lean heavily on Henry, a four-year varsity starter, for scoring, along with Keating and Dowell.
"Getting back to the fundamentals," Jackson said Caroline's key to success. "Rebounding, boxing out, good passes. The basics. So far I've loved what I've seen in preseason. The girls are buying in. There are some things we need to improve on, but the girls are working hard."
NORTH DORCHESTER
Head Coach: Dontele Pinder.
Who's Where: Remedy Wongus (So., G/F); Areinya Taylor (Sr., G); Ziya Patton (Sr., F); Diamond Newbill (Fr., G); Sammir Holland (Fr., G); Destiny Wongus (Fr., G).
Outlook: An assistant at Colonel Richardson the past eight seasons, Pinder begins his first head coaching job with plenty of optimism.
"I feel like we have a great core group," Pinder said. "We're kind of in the middle of the transition, where we have some of our key seniors that are leading, but we have a good group of freshmen that I feel like are going to be productive in the beginning. I'm excited and I think they're excited about the change. Hopefully we can make some noise here in the North."
QUEEN ANNE'S
Head Coach: Mike Kern.
Who's Where: Damya Henry (Jr., G); Cheyanne Hollis (Jr., F/C); Bea Holthaus (So., F); Laila Coles (So., G); Kariana Hickson (So., G); Taylor Jordan (So., G); RJ Ensor (Sr., G); Lucy Taylor (Sr., C); Sydney Pinder (Jr., F); Keilah Reed (Jr., G); Abby Robinson (So., G); Dillon Simpler (So., G); Lex Kern (So., G).
Outlook: With practically everyone back from last season, as well as the additions of Hollis and Henry, it's not surprising Kern thinks the potential is there to do well at the state level, if Queen Anne's can advance out of the region.
"We've never had a team that can all shoot," Kern said. "We've had teams where we had one true shooter and that's it. We might have a kid who could drive. We had Kendall Moxey (Queen Anne's career leading scorer) who could play the post. But we've never had a solid (team) that can shoot from so many different area's of the court."
That's a combination that could have the Lions driving deep into another postseason.
ST. MICHAELS
Head Coach: Jonathan Matthews.
Who's Where: Jordyn Beckett (So., F/C); Hanna Corkran (So., F/C); Aleah George (So., F); Rebeca Martinez (Jr., G); Evelyn Mautz (Fr., G); Kayla Montoya (So. SG); Olivia Patrick (Jr., G/F); Alayna Porter (Fr., G); Maddisyn Roe (Jr., G); Bella Simmons (Fr., G); Kendall Rosenberger (So., C); Tess Weller (Jr., PG); Shayla Frink (Jr., C); Kaelyn Hicks (Fr., G/F); Maleia Loffland (Fr., G).
Outlook: Another former Colonel Richardson assistant, Matthews begins his first head coaching job hoping to build on what former head coach Mark Potter started.
"Mark gave us a good start from last year for the ninth graders that are 10th graders this year," Matthews said. "We're still working on some of our developmental things, but I think in the long run we'll be all right. I have high hopes for them."
SAINTS PETER & PAUL
Head Coach: Katie Murphy.
Who's Where: Avery McCall (Jr., F/C); Annie Albright (Jr., G); Lucy Rankin (Jr., G/F); Hazel Spurry (Jr., G); Emma Hainey (So., G); Kaylin Palmer (So., F/C); Bridget Gilman (So., G); Tara Foley (So., G/F); Ryleigh Briddell (So., C/F); Veronica Pool (So., G); Natalee Lyons (Fr., G); Caroline Jallade (Fr., C/F).
Outlook: While the Sabres and Delmarva Christian have met for the Eastern Shore Independent Athletic Conference title the last three seasons, Murphy thinks this season could be more wide open with Worcester Prep, Gunston and Salisbury School pushing to improve.
"Everyone is a threat," Murphy said.
Murphy admits it's been somewhat hard to gauge her team's potential because she hasn't had her full lineup for games or practices.
And though the losses of Morgan Quade (graduation) and Sam Murphy (transfer) will hurt, the Sabres have a solid core with McCall, Albright, Rankin, Hainey and the continuing emergence of Palmer and Gilman.
"We finally have everybody back and we're working on a few things to find out who those (starting) five are," Murphy said. "They want to learn. They want to get better. Working together as a team is where we are right now."

title: TC Shore goes unbeaten at USFHA Festival
author: Bill Haufe
content:
TC Shore goes unbeaten at USFHA Festival

 December 5, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 493
 Words 

 Read News Document

 There have always been goals.The foremost were to play good field hockey and give area high school players a chance to be seen by college coaches.
Debbie McQuaid has done this for 28 years during Thanksgiving weekend, taking area teams to the annual United States Field Hockey Association Festival in locations in Florida, California and Arizona.
"I don't really care about the win-loss (record)," McQuaid said. "But winning is always fun."
Well, McQuaid and her TC Shore team had a lot of fun last weekend, as it went 5-0 over three days of pool play during the annual USFHA Festival at the Paradise Coast Sports Complex in Naples, Florida.
"We've won our pool a couple of times," McQuaid said. "But we've never gone 5-0. It was very exciting."
It was also very impressive, considering after Friday's tournament-opening 5-2 victory over Team Gateway of St. Louis, TC Shore yielded only one more goal over its remaining four games.
"Somebody asked me, 'Well, who stood out?'" McQuaid said. "I said, 'None of them and all of them.' They just worked as a unit. And they were so supportive. We had (Saints Peter and Paul eighth-grader) Caroline (Corson) being younger and they were just all so supportive of her. Just nice to see. No egos."
TC Shore also won its second game Friday, as Queen Anne's County High goalies Cassidy Alexander and Caroline Kimball combined for a 3-0 shutout of Xcaliber (New Jersey). It was after Day 1, that McQuaid — who is currently the head coach at Sts. Peter and Paul, but has also been head coach at St. Michaels and Easton — thought her team could go undefeated.
"Those were the two best teams," McQuaid said of Team Gateway and Xcaliber.
TC Shore came back to post back-to-back shutouts on Saturday, blanking both GOA Canada and Atlanta by 3-0 finals. In addition to Kimball and Alexander not letting anything get past them, the play of backs and midfielders Ellee McLean (Queen Anne's), Haley Cole (Queen Anne's), Angie Webb (SSPP), Jordan Bilbo (Queen Anne's), Kadence McGuckin (Easton) and Claire Bieber (SSPP) stymied opponents.
"The midfield really took care of things. They locked them down," McQuaid said.
TC Shore also had Gunston's Layla Kent and Grace Shepherd, who saw time up front, at midfield, and in the back. McQuaid, who was assisted by Missy Cannon and Julie Corson, had Sadie Latchaw (Kent Island), Ella Napier (Kent Island) and Sadie Jacobs (SSPP) rotating at midfield and forward, and Jules Stepp (SSPP), Ryann Quicke (Easton) and Gabi Shepherd (Gunston) up front. That offensive group combined to outscore the opposition, 15-3, for the tournament.
TC Shore punctuated its unbeaten run Sunday with a 2-1 victory over HTC of Connecticut.
"We started probably three years ago with the core group and they stayed together through Disney tournaments and spring tournaments," McQuaid said. "And basically they just trust each other. Their personalities get along on the field, off the field. It was just a joy to coach. They enjoy themselves on the field."

title: Wicomico defeats Easton
author: Bill Haufe
content:
Wicomico defeats Easton

 December 11, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Bill Haufe | Section: Sports 
 
 577
 Words 

 Read News Document

 EASTON — Jason Biringer has no illusion of flipping Easton High's wrestling program around overnight."It's growing pains," said Biringer, who has returned as the Warriors head coach after three seasons away from the program. "We set small goals for each of these guys. Hey, sometimes it might be just, get through the first period for those super raw new guys. After that we just keep building a little more. Make it through your first match. Get your first win. Get another win. Small steps."
Biringer saw some of his green roster take some small steps Wednesday night during a 58-24 loss to Wicomico, which won four of the five varsity matches wrestled to go along with six forfeit wins.
"We know we have to work," said Biringer, whose roster of 30 has only six wrestlers with more experience than just this season. "And we know there's a lot to do, and a lot of ways to get better. But I'm happy with the effort they are putting in. Like I said, it's a lot to ask."
Wicomico had an 18-6 lead via three forfeits through the first four weight classes, then extended that cushion to 24-6, when Deion Finney pinned AJ Matulay in 1 minute, 4 seconds at 132 pounds.
Easton (0-2) picked up its lone win not by way of forfeit at 138, when Shawn Arnold fell into a 3-0 first-period hole, scored a late escape, then pinned Ethan Brewington at 2:39, pulling the Warriors within 24-12.
"Shawn is a scrappy kid," Biringer said. "We've been working with him. He's got a high octane motor. Getting him to be settle down and be more controlled out there, that's our focus. But he has a ton of potential. He's a second-year kid. Bright future for him if he keeps working hard."
The Indians won the other three matches that were wrestled, the tightest being at 144, where Corey Richardson decisioned Easton's Adonis Schmitt, 7-2. Wi-Hi's Adelson Theajeon pinned Anthony Melendez in 2:45 at 175, and Keven Mondestin got a 21-second fall over Matthew Brunner at 285.
"Those guys who wrestled, we're asking a lot of those kids," Biringer said. "Wi-Hi also has experience. They have a good program. (Head coach) Nate Stone's been there for many years now and always has a solid group."
Wicomico's Terry Scott (106), Tavenon Outlaw (120), Davidson Fortunel (126), Rowan Okerblom (157), Cameron Wawrzenak (165) and Jamier Johnson (215) each won by forfeit.
"We've got a core of guys that have several years of experience, but they are all kind of lumped down in like in the lower weights," Stone said. "But we have a bunch of guys we think are going to do really well. Overall I thought our conditioning was pretty good for it being this early (in the season). And we didn't look super sloppy. So fundamentally we did OK."
Easton's other wins came via forfeit from Estaben Velasquez (113), Matthew Bravo (150) and Wahaab Popal (190).
"We're focused on each individual's production," said Biringer, who was also encouraged by his girls winning three of five matches, and his boys winning three of the seven junior-varsity bouts. "Lot of youth. Almost exclusively sophomores and freshmen, and then a few juniors and two seniors.
"And the kids have had a good attitude," Biringer added. "They're trying. They want to learn the moves. They want to get better. It takes showing up and putting in that work every day. It's a sport of experience and you have to have the long view."

title: Star Democrat's new reporter: Ahmad Garnett is here to listen
author: Veronica Fernandez-Alvarado
content:
Star Democrat's new reporter: Ahmad Garnett is here to listen

 December 24, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Veronica Fernandez-Alvarado | Section: News 
 
 425
 Words 

 Read News Document

 EASTON — Ahmad Garnett, a recently hired reporter at the Star Democrat, is a native Marylander from Prince George's County, and he is eager to explore the rich tapestry of stories on the Eastern Shore.Garnett will be covering Caroline County and is excited to learn all the ins and outs of the county.
Before readers go looking for his byline, there is a bit to know about the new hire. Garnett is sports-centered, outgoing and incredibly curious, and has loved news since he was a child.
Garnett came to journalism through his family's love for sports. Growing up, alongside his brothers, he would join his father in looking at newspapers for any news on his favorite team, the Washington Commanders.
In those moments together, his family would read about who was going to make the team, who got cut and other news.
"I started hearing sports broadcasters on the radio and on TV and then video games," Garnett said. "And I was just like, 'this is something I want to get into, like sports media.' And when I got older, and (my interests) started to transition more into news on social media… I knew what I pretty much wanted to do since I was in middle school. I knew I wanted to be a reporter in some capacity."
After high school, Garnett attended Norfolk State University for its strong mass communications program and, in part, because it was his father's alma mater.
Garnett said his favorite part of being a reporter is the ability to provide service to other people. He describes a specific joy that people have when they see a story about themselves for the first time.
"I remember when I first started covering at school, one of the athletes came up to me and was like, 'Hey, you write for the school newspaper?' And I was like, 'yeah,' and he said 'that was a great story you did.' And that was the first time I ever had somebody come up to me and tell me they enjoyed my work," Garnett said.
Garmett said now as a reporter for the Star Democrat he is excited to do thorough and good work for the people of the Eastern Shore.
He encourages anyone eager to tell their story or a story of the area to reach out to him.
"We could talk about sports or we could talk about what's going on in your community, and where you have problems, and where you see issues," Garnett said. "There's always a story everywhere, so I don't want anybody to think 'this is a bad story.'"
